articles.title: Cruise Ships and Container Huts: Asian Games 2026 Faces Bed Crunch Before Liftoff
articles.excerpt: With 17,000 athletes and officials descending on Nagoya and Aichi — more than the Olympics — organizers have scrapped the athletes' village for a cruise liner, hotels and wooden containers, and not everyone is sleeping easy.
articles.image_caption: Replica container accommodation built by the Sports Authority of India. Indian athletes are spending nights in the units to acclimatize before the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora fans get a record-sized Indian contingent and the tantalizing prospect of an India-Pakistan cricket final on a global stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Cricket Bat to Shotgun: At 50, Mairaj Ahmad Khan Chases Asian Games Glory
articles.excerpt: India's first Olympic skeet shooter — a former Uttar Pradesh cricketer who once batted alongside a young Virender Sehwag — heads to Aichi-Nagoya for his fourth Asian Games, still chasing a first Asiad medal.
articles.image_caption: Skeet shooter Mairaj Ahmad Khan. The 50-year-old will compete at his fourth Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, still chasing a first Asiad medal.
articles.nri_angle: A longevity story that resonates with diaspora sports fans — and a reminder of the unconventional pathways India's veteran athletes still carve at the highest level.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Varun Chakaravarthy Ruled Out of Afghanistan T20Is With Side Strain
articles.excerpt: Scans revealed the side strain after Sunday's opener in Delhi; Ravi Bishnoi comes into the XI and Chakaravarthy's Asian Games availability is now in doubt.

sources.label: OurNet/IANS (ruled out, doubtful for Asian Games)

articles.nri_angle: Indian cricket's injury carousel is followed intensely by the diaspora — and the Asian Games squad implications matter to fans planning to follow India's Japan campaign.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gukesh and Team India Stranded Five Hours Over Samarkand Hotel Chaos
articles.excerpt: Captain Srinath Narayanan slammed the FIDE arrangements on X after the defending champions landed to find no rooms and no answers, a day before the Olympiad begins.
articles.image_caption: Indian grandmasters at the chessboard during a tournament. The Indian contingent was stranded for five hours on arrival in Samarkand after their hotel rooms were not allotted.
articles.nri_angle: Indian chess is a diaspora pride story — Gukesh's world title and the 2024 double gold made the team a household name among Indian families abroad, who follow the Olympiad closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mukesh Kumar joins Nottinghamshire for title-chasing County Championship run-in
articles.excerpt: India seamer Mukesh Kumar has signed with Nottinghamshire for the final two games of the 2026 County Championship season, with the club sitting four points behind leaders Somerset in the Division One title race.
articles.image_caption: Indian seamer Mukesh Kumar, who has signed with Nottinghamshire for the final two County Championship fixtures.
articles.nri_angle: An India international in a Division One title race gives British Asian cricket fans — and the large South Asian community around Trent Bridge — a live stake in the English county season's closing act.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kranti Gaud Fined 10% of Match Fee for Send-Off in Women's Asia Cup Final
articles.excerpt: The India pacer was docked part of her match fee and handed one demerit point for gesturing opener Imesha Dulani toward the pavilion during Sunday's final against Sri Lanka in Dubai.
articles.image_caption: Kranti Gaud with the Indian women's cricket team during a group photograph with the Prime Minister in New Delhi. Gaud was fined 10% of her match fee for a send-off to Sri Lanka opener Imesha Dulani during the Women's T20 Asia Cup final in Dubai.
articles.nri_angle: India's 72-run final win over Sri Lanka thrilled South Asian diaspora fans, and the Dubai final — played before a large expatriate crowd — put women's cricket's rising diaspora audience and the tightening policing of send-offs squarely in the spotlight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sharma's 82 off 32 seals seven-wicket T20 win over Afghanistan
articles.excerpt: Abhishek Sharma smashed 82 off 32 balls to power India's 13.4-over chase at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, taking a 1-0 series lead. Omarzai's 64 lifted Afghanistan to 156/8.
articles.image_caption: The Feroz Shah Kotla, now known as the Arun Jaitley Stadium, in New Delhi during a match. India chased down 157 in 13.4 overs there to beat Afghanistan by seven wickets in the first T20I.
articles.nri_angle: A 13.4-over chase led by Abhishek Sharma's 82 gave diaspora fans a fast, highlight-filled evening, and young stars like Sharma and Tilak Varma are building a global following with two days to the second T20I.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Refuse Asia Cup Trophy From Naqvi Again After Women's Team Wins Final
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's side beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in Dubai to win an eighth Women's Asia Cup, then stayed away from the presentation stage as ACC president Mohsin Naqvi waited — repeating the men's team's 2025 stand.
articles.image_caption: ACC president Mohsin Naqvi at the stadium during the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai. India's players stayed away from the presentation stage as he waited to hand over the trophy.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora fans in Dubai drove the 'trophy chor' chants, and Indian communities in the US, UK, and Canada woke up split online between celebrating the team's principle and arguing sport should stay separate from politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gavaskar Slams Domestic Format: 'How Does a Team Learn to Take 20 Wickets?'
articles.excerpt: In his Mid-Day column, the batting legend cited the Duleep Trophy final — where East Zone batted on and shook hands instead of pushing for an outright win — to explain India's Test struggles.
articles.image_caption: Sunil Gavaskar. The former India captain questioned how teams can learn to take 20 wickets under the current domestic format.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora fans who watch India struggle to finish sides on flat pitches will recognize Gavaskar's diagnosis: domestic cricket rewards batting longer, not bowling better, and the Test side inherits the habit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: KL Rahul in Line for ODI Vice-Captaincy as Asian Games Clash Hits India's Plans
articles.excerpt: With Shreyas Iyer leading India at the Asian Games in Japan, the vice-captaincy under Shubman Gill is open for the September 27 ODI series — and the second wicketkeeper slot has become a Pant vs Jurel debate.
articles.image_caption: KL Rahul trains with the Indian cricket team wearing the blue India kit and helmet. He is the front-runner to be named India vice-captain for the three-match ODI series against the West Indies.
articles.nri_angle: A home ODI series with Kohli back and a new-look India is primetime diaspora viewing, and the Asian Games overlap means fans get two Indian teams playing on different continents in the same week.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tanvi Patri, 15, Wins U17 Crown in All-Indian Final at Asia Junior Championships
articles.excerpt: The 15-year-old from Odisha beat compatriot Shaina Manimuthu 11-15, 15-10, 15-12 in Chengdu, capping a breakthrough 2026 season that already includes her first international title.
articles.nri_angle: Another Indian teenager winning Asian age-group titles against Chinese and Japanese competition strengthens the junior pipeline diaspora fans are watching as the senior women's singles ranks need fresh faces.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nepal Beat UAE to Win ACC Premier Cup and Book Asia Cup 2027 Spot
articles.excerpt: Aasif Sheikh's century and Gulsan Jha's late assault powered Nepal to 313, before Karan KC and Lalit Rajbanshi derailed a UAE chase anchored by Rahul Chopra's unbeaten hundred at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur.
articles.image_caption: Nepal's players celebrate with the trophy and a champions banner after winning the ACC Men's Premier Cup 2026 final. Nepal beat the UAE by 44 runs in Kuala Lumpur to seal qualification for the Asia Cup 2027.
articles.nri_angle: The UAE's squad is stacked with Indian-origin players, including captain Harpreet Singh Bhatia and centurion Rahul Chopra, highlighting the diaspora's role in Gulf cricket.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harleen Deol Joins Barbados Tridents for Remainder of WCPL 2026
articles.excerpt: The 28-year-old India batter becomes the fifth Indian in this year's Women's Caribbean Premier League, linking up with Kiran Navgire and Pooja Vastrakar for her first global franchise stint.
articles.image_caption: Harleen Deol celebrates with the Indian flag after India’s ODI World Cup triumph in 2025. The 28-year-old batter has signed with the Barbados Tridents for the remainder of the WCPL 2026 season.
articles.nri_angle: A fifth Indian joins the Caribbean league, with three Indians now in the defending champions' squad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rajeev Ram Retires After US Open Semifinal Loss, Ending Storied Doubles Career
articles.excerpt: The former world No. 1 doubles star played his final match alongside Joe Salisbury on September 11, then gave a tearful on-court farewell honoring his late father.
articles.image_caption: Rajeev Ram receives a commemorative frame during his on-court farewell ceremony at the US Open. The former doubles world No. 1 retired after playing his final match on September 11, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The greatest Indian-American tennis player of all time says goodbye at the tournament where he built his legacy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Afghanistan vs India T20Is: Full Schedule, Squads and How to Watch
articles.excerpt: Three T20 internationals at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17 — Afghanistan's first series as host against India, with Jasprit Bumrah back in India's squad.
articles.image_caption: India players gather in a huddle during a T20I match, wearing the team blue kit sponsored by Apollo Tyres. India face Afghanistan in a three-match T20I series at Delhis Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The series sits at the intersection of two of cricket's most followed fan bases — the Indian and Afghan diasporas in the UK, North America and the Gulf — with morning start times in North America making the games easy to follow live.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Babar Azam Enters Record Books With 2,000 WTC Runs as Captain
articles.excerpt: The Pakistan captain's 76 at Edgbaston made him the fourth batter — and second Asian — to reach 2,000 World Test Championship runs as captain, a milestone that eluded India's Kohli and Rohit. But England completed a 3-0 whitewash.
articles.image_caption: Babar Azam. The former Pakistan captain became only the fourth captain to score 2,000 runs in the World Test Championship, reaching the milestone at Edgbaston.
articles.nri_angle: A record that eluded Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma as captains gives subcontinent cricket fans — including millions in the diaspora — a fresh statistical lens on Babar Azam's standing, even as Pakistan's tour ended in a 3-0 whitewash.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bumrah Finds Rhythm in Delhi Nets Ahead of Afghanistan T20I Return
articles.excerpt: Bowling at full intensity in Thursday's Delhi nets, Jasprit Bumrah looked ready for his first T20I since March. Shreyas Iyer wants him to get game time; Afghanistan say they have a plan for him.
articles.image_caption: Jasprit Bumrah. The pacer bowled at full intensity in the Delhi nets on Thursday as he closes in on a T20I return against Afghanistan.
articles.nri_angle: Bumrah's injury comeback is the biggest storyline in Indian cricket for diaspora fans, and the Afghanistan series — played entirely in Delhi — offers a rare home-format tune-up before the Asian Games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Divyanshi Choudhary Breaks Down After Last-Minute Asian Games Wushu Axing
articles.excerpt: The 18-year-old wushu player beat Roshibina Devi in the selection trials and had already collected her India kit for Aichi-Nagoya — then was dropped days before departure, citing a knee injury her camp calls treatable.
articles.image_caption: Sanda competition. Divyanshi Choudhary, 18, was dropped from India's Asian Games 2026 squad in the women's 60kg Sanda category days before departure.
articles.nri_angle: Selection transparency and athlete welfare in Indian sports — a governance issue diaspora fans follow closely as India chases medals beyond cricket at the Asian Games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anmol Ekka Double Fires India Into Fourth Straight Junior Asia Cup Final
articles.excerpt: India beat Malaysia 3-1 in Moqi, China, with captain Ekka scoring twice and goalkeeper Vivek Lakra saving a penalty stroke; South Korea await in Sunday's final.
articles.image_caption: India's junior men's hockey team in action. Anmol Ekka's double fired the defending champions into a fourth straight Junior Asia Cup final.
articles.nri_angle: Anmol Ekka's 16-goal breakout gives diaspora hockey fans a new star to follow as India's junior pipeline builds toward the Junior World Cup.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New Zealand Tour Sells 50,000 Tickets in Two Weeks
articles.excerpt: NZ Cricket sold more than 50,000 tickets in just over two weeks for India's first tour in six years, reopening Eden Park's sixth tier for the first time since 2019.
articles.image_caption: A packed cricket stadium under lights during a night match. Tickets for India's tour of New Zealand sold 50,000 seats within two weeks.
articles.nri_angle: India fixtures draw the largest and loudest diaspora crowds of any touring side in New Zealand, home to one of the world's fastest-growing Indian communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kuldeep Yadav's Career-Best Ten-For Powers Yorkshire to Innings Win Over Essex
articles.excerpt: The India wrist-spinner's 10 for 120 — his first ten-wicket haul in first-class cricket — sank Essex twice at Headingley and all but sealed Yorkshire's Division One survival.
articles.image_caption: Kuldeep Yadav during a visit to the Prime Minister's Office in New Delhi. Yadav took a career-best ten-wicket haul for Yorkshire in their innings win over Essex.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cricket fans in England watched a home hero dominate at Headingley, and Kuldeep's county form is being closely tracked in India ahead of future tours.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shami Breaks Silence on India Absence, Sets Sights on Comeback
articles.excerpt: Marking his 100th first-class match with a Duleep Trophy title, the 36-year-old pacer says his eyes are on the "next level" — as selectors insist they stayed in touch through his England-tour absence.
articles.image_caption: Mohammed Shami after receiving the Arjuna Award. Shami has broken his silence on his absence from the India squad and says he is targeting a comeback.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora cricket fans and US club/community players follow Shami's comeback push as the national team's most decorated active quick.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Zealand Captain Santner Turns Down Big BBL Deal to Lead Against India
articles.excerpt: The 34-year-old rejected a two-year Adelaide Strikers offer to keep his New Zealand central contract and white-ball captaincy ahead of the India home series.
articles.nri_angle: The India vs New Zealand home series is the marquee event Santner prioritised — directly relevant to the Indian cricket diaspora, which follows the fixture intensely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Women's Spinners Bundle Pakistan Out for 55 in Asia Cup Rout
articles.excerpt: Left-arm spinner Shree Charani's 3 for 7 led a spin masterclass in Dubai, and Harmanpreet Kaur sealed a seven-wicket win in 8.4 overs in her 150th T20I as captain.
articles.nri_angle: India-Pakistan cricket is appointment viewing for the South Asian diaspora, and this rout gave fans across the US, Canada, UK and the Gulf a night to savour.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tanya Chaudhary Smashes National Hammer Throw Record Days Before Asian Games
articles.excerpt: The Uttar Pradesh athlete sent the hammer to 68.35m at the Indian Athletics Series Final on Thursday, breaking 18-year-old Anushka Yadav's record with the Aichi-Nagoya Games beginning September 19.
articles.nri_angle: India's rising women's hammer throw, led by Chaudhary and Yadav, gives diaspora track fans a genuine medal hope at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Georgia Teen Anannya Aneesh Earns Spot at 2027 U19 Women's World Cup
articles.excerpt: The Mountain View High School senior helped the USA Women's U19 team sweep the Americas Qualifier to reach the 2027 ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup.
articles.nri_angle: Aneesh's arc — falling in love with cricket through the IPL with her father in Georgia, representing the USA, and planning to play in India — runs the full arc of the diaspora cricket dream.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Rout Pakistan 19-0 to Storm Into Junior Women's Hockey Asia Cup Semis
articles.excerpt: India's junior women thrashed Pakistan 19-0 in their Women's Junior Asia Cup quarterfinal in Moqi, China — Pooja Malik hit a hat-trick and the defending champions, now two wins from a third straight continental title, face the South Korea-Malaysia winner in the semifinals.
articles.image_caption: Action from the India-Pakistan match at the Women's Junior Asia Cup in Moqi, China. India won the quarterfinal 19-0 to storm into the semifinals.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families whose kids play field hockey in US and Canadian leagues, this junior side — defending champions now two wins from a three-peat — is the next generation to watch, with several of these names likely to step into the senior India squad within a year or two.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bumrah Included, Yash Thakur Replaces Harshit Rana in India T20I Squads
articles.excerpt: The BCCI on Thursday named Vidarbha pacer Yash Thakur as Harshit Rana's replacement for the Afghanistan T20Is and the 2026 Asian Games after Rana suffered a rectus femoris strain during a match simulation, while Jasprit Bumrah, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar all made the cut.
articles.image_caption: India fast bowler Yash Thakur trains with the national squad. The 27-year-old Vidarbha pacer was named as Harshit Rana's replacement for the Afghanistan T20Is and the 2026 Asian Games.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian fans in the US, UK and Canada who follow the team through late-night streams and diaspora watch parties, a settled pace attack — Bumrah back, Thakur blooded — sets the tone for the home season and the Asian Games campaign in Nagoya.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Antim Panghal Confident as India Targets Wrestling Gold at Asian Games
articles.excerpt: The women's 53kg wrestler says a senior-junior mix, three months of joint training and a Japanese coach have the squad ready for Aichi-Nagoya.
articles.image_caption: Two wrestlers grapple on the mat during a bout. Antim Panghal heads into the Asian Games as one of India’s leading medal hopes in wrestling.
articles.nri_angle: The Asian Games are a marquee quadrennial event for the diaspora's sporting calendar, and wrestling remains one of the disciplines where Indian fans abroad expect podium finishes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Firm Favourites as Bangladesh Eye Upset in Women's Asia Cup Semi-Final
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's unbeaten side meet Bangladesh in Dubai on Thursday, chasing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title.
articles.image_caption: Players from India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Pakistan in a Women’s Asia Cup 2026 semi-final graphic. India face Bangladesh in the last-four clash.
articles.nri_angle: The 8 PM IST start (7:30 AM Pacific) makes this a morning watch for the US diaspora, with SonyLIV and Sony Max carrying the game for Indian fans abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vinicius Jr and Raphinha Headline Brazil Squad for Historic First Friendly in India
articles.excerpt: Carlo Ancelotti named a 26-man squad for the October 3 fixture at Salt Lake Stadium — his first since Brazil's World Cup exit, and a clear changing of the guard.
articles.image_caption: Brazil forward Vinicius Jr celebrates in the national team colours. Vinicius and Raphinha headline Brazil’s squad for their historic first friendly on Indian soil.
articles.nri_angle: The first-ever Brazil-India fixture gives football-mad Kolkata a landmark night and draws the Indian diaspora's large global football audience toward the Indian game.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: East Zone One Day From Duleep Trophy Glory as Kishan Shines Again
articles.excerpt: East Zone closed day four of the Duleep Trophy final at 212 for 5, a 584-run lead over South Zone, with Ishan Kishan's second-innings 80 following his 270 and leaving a first title in 14 years within reach.
articles.image_caption: Ishan Kishan. The wicketkeeper-batter starred for East Zone as they closed in on Duleep Trophy glory.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora cricket fans following Ishan Kishan's comeback get another signal that his India recall case is building at Chepauk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hardik Pandya Named in India A Squad for Australia A Home Series in Puducherry
articles.excerpt: The all-rounder, who has not played competitive cricket since IPL 2026, has been included in the one-day squad subject to fitness clearance as India plan his return ahead of the ODI World Cup.
articles.image_caption: Indian cricketer Hardik Pandya. The all-rounder has been named in the India A squad for the home series against Australia A in Puducherry.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cricket fans across the diaspora are closely tracking Pandya's fitness comeback, with the all-rounder seen as pivotal to India's ODI World Cup campaign in 2027.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
